name: Reasoning and Decision-Making
summary: The prefrontal cortex weighs options, simulates outcomes, and integrates information into a coherent plan.
description: The dorsolateral prefrontal cortex manages working memory — holding multiple pieces of information simultaneously while manipulating them. Decision-making involves accumulation of evidence — neural populations represent competing options, and their firing rates gradually build up. When one reaches a threshold, the decision is made. The anterior cingulate cortex monitors for conflicts between competing responses. The basal ganglia evaluate the expected reward of different actions. Much of this processing is unconscious. Studies show that the brain often 'decides' before you're consciously aware — raising profound questions about the nature of free will.
